chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu al-Jaroud, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

I heard Amir al-Mu-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) saying upon the pulpit: 'O group of businessmen! Jurisprudence, then the business! Jurisprudence, then the business! Jurisprudence, then the business! By Allah, usury in this community is more hidden than the creeping of an ant on a dark rock. Mix your oaths with truthfulness. The merchant who is immoral is in the Fire, except for the one who takes the right and gives the right.'

key_terms.أَيْمَانَكُمْ: Your oaths; sworn statements in trade
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Dark rock; a type of stone, used here to illustrate hiddenness
key_terms.الْفَاجِرُ: The immoral/sinner; one who transgresses religious bounds

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between jurisprudence and trade in Shia Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) addresses merchants, emphasizing that understanding jurisprudence (fiqh) is a prerequisite for engaging in trade. He warns that usury (riba) is subtle and prevalent, urging traders to ensure their oaths are truthful, and states that immoral merchants will be in Hellfire unless they deal justly by taking what is rightfully theirs and giving what is due.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from usman Bin Isa, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Al Asbagh Bin Nubata who said,

‘I heard Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> saying upon the Pulpit: ‘O group of businessmen! The jurisprudence, then the business! The jurisprudence, then the business! The jurisprudence, then the business! By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The interest (usury) in this community is more hidden than the footsteps of the ant upon the dark rock. Immerse your beliefs with the truthfulness. If the business man is an immoral, then immoral is in the Fire except for the one who takes the right and gives the right’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from abu al-Jarud from al-Asbagh Nubatah who has said the following: “

I heard Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying from the pulpit, ‘O people who do business, you must learn fiqh (laws), then go in business, you must learn fiqh (laws) then go in business, you must learn fiqh (laws) then go in business. I swear by Allah, Riba ’ creeps in this nation more quietly than an ant’s moving on a hard and smooth rock. Blend your belief with truthfulness. A sinful business person is a criminal, and a criminal person is in the fire except those who take what is right and give what is right.’”
